chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Jamil from Zurarah from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
"The waiting period (iddah) and menstruation for women, if she claims it, is accepted (she is believed)." And this report does not contradict what has been narrated

key_terms.اَلْعِدَّةُ: The waiting period (iddah) a woman must observe after divorce or death of husband before remarriage
key_terms.صُدِّقَتْ: She is believed/accepted (legal principle of accepting testimony)

ai.seo_question: What is the legal ruling on a woman's claim of menstruation or waiting period in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: In the context of *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq establishes the principle of *al-istishab* (presumption of continuity) or *al-bara'a* (presumption of innocence) in personal status cases, prioritizing the woman's testimony regarding her *iddah* (waiting period) and *hayd* (menstruation) to resolve marital uncertainty. This ruling is particularly significant in Shia jurisprudence for facilitating the ease of remarriage and clarifying lineage, provided no contradictory evidence is presented. It underscores the reliability of female testimony in matters of personal biological status, a key component of *fiqh al-nisa* (jurisprudence of women).
